A straight-on photograph of a small international bookshop's window display at dusk, shot on a 50mm lens with the glass filling most of the frame and the warm interior glowing behind it.

Taped to the inside of the glass are five separate printed signs, each in a different script, all flat to the glass, all crisply legible and correctly spelled.

At the top centre, the largest sign is white card with black type reading "WORLD LITERATURE" in bold sans-serif capitals. Directly beneath it, a smaller cream sign carries the Russian words "КНИГИ И КОФЕ" in dark red capitals. To the left of centre, a pale blue sign carries the Japanese characters "本屋" in heavy black brushed strokes, with the smaller Latin word "HONYA" printed beneath them. To the right of centre, a mustard yellow sign carries the Chinese characters "新書到" in black, with a thin black border around the card. In the lower left corner of the window, a small handwritten white sign in blue ink reads "OUVERT" above a second line reading "10h - 19h".

Behind the glass, three wooden shelves are stacked with books seen mostly spine-on, their titles too small to resolve into words, in muted reds, greens and creams. A brass desk lamp with a green glass shade sits on the middle shelf, throwing warm light upward. A tortoiseshell cat sleeps curled on a stack of four large books on the bottom shelf. In the upper right of the glass, the reflection of a streetlight and the dim silhouette of a passing cyclist appear as a partial overlay on the scene, clearly reading as a reflection on the glass rather than as objects inside the shop.

The pavement in front is wet and reflects a little of the window's warm light. Each of the five signs remains individually sharp and readable, with no script bleeding into another and no invented characters.
